I would keep the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, I know this system fits my land, my water conditions, and the local market better than trying something risky. At the start of the growing season, I would carry the winter wheat through to harvest first, then I would follow immediately with summer maize. I would use improved wheat seed because it is steady and easier for me to manage, and I would use hybrid maize because the yield is usually better and worth the extra seed cost. For tillage, I would rotary-till before maize after wheat harvest because it is fast and practical for me; for wheat, I would mostly stay with rotary tillage too because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing every year. For fertilizer, I would put enough nitrogen on both crops to secure yield, with phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels since I still want strong roots and grain filling. For water, I would irrigate wheat more times because spring here is often dry, while maize would usually need fewer irrigations if the summer rains come normally. I would not spray excessively, but I would still do a few pesticide applications on each crop because I do not want weeds, aphids, rust, corn borer, or leaf diseases to cut yield. Since no land size was given, I am making this plan for 10 mu total, split across the same land in two seasons.
